note: Declares WHAT speech the game needs, not how it is made. The pipeline never discovers work by scanning code — if it is not declared here it is not generated. See tools/speech/README.md.

word.note: Every vocabulary word across all seven difficulty tiers. Only the 'word' field is read — the emoji is a picture hint on screen and never reaches a recording. Grapheme markers are stripped, so MOU[CH]A is recorded as moucha. Sent lowercase: an all-capitals word invites the model to spell it out.
word.phrase_note: Multi-word entries are announced as the child crosses each space — THIS, THIS IS, THIS IS GOOD. Those partials are not recorded separately: the full phrase is played and stopped at a word boundary, so every stage sounds like the same reading rather than a fresh one. Boundaries come from `align`.

ui.note: Spoken UI text, split from its translation templates on the %s placeholders. Recorded in the UI language, which is often not the learning language — the recap is one sentence built from both.
ui.synthesis_note: Recorded one request at a time, never cut from a sheet. These fragments are short function words and a sheet of them has gaps between items no bigger than the gaps inside them, which is the one case sheet cutting cannot survive: the first Czech attempt merged two and shifted every later cut by one, and German repeated it exactly when its profile was added without the override. The rule lives here so a new language inherits it. Carrier words come from the voice profile, since they must be words of that language.

number_form.note: Numbers in the grammatical form the recap frame requires, spoken in the UI language. Recorded only where that differs from the citation form, so a language that does not inflect records none of them. A language with no entry in data/number_forms.json, or an empty one, records nothing here and keeps using the plain number — which is correct for English, German, Dutch, the Scandinavian languages and the Romance ones. Czech, Slovak, Polish, Ukrainian, Greek, Finnish, Hungarian and Turkish will all need it.

master_format.note: What the provider returns and what is archived. Lossless, so the shipped bitrate can change without paying to resynthesise.

ship_format.note: What goes in the AAB. Revisit only after the Phase 3 A/B listening test on a TV.

processing.note: Any change here restages every clip for re-encoding, because it changes the audio — but only re-encoding, from the archived masters. It never costs a synthesis credit. Bump the version deliberately.
processing.levelling_note: Mean RMS with a peak ceiling, not EBU R128. Integrated loudness needs a window a letter name does not have — 'bé' is under 400ms and loudnorm measures it as -inf. One target for the whole voice family also keeps the batch consistent, which matters more here than any single clip hitting a number.
processing.internal_silence_note: A pause inside a clip is not a cutting error — the model really did pause — but 1.35 seconds between 'ocean' and 'wave' is a clip that sounds finished while it is still playing. Only silence with sound on both sides is shortened; the ends are the trimmer's job. Clips with nothing to shorten re-encode byte-identically, which is how the re-listen can be limited to what actually changed.
processing.alignment_note: Forced alignment supplies the word boundaries inside a phrase. The sheet's own alignment cannot: it is right at the ends of a sheet and drifts by over a second in the middle. A clip whose alignment loss exceeds this is left without boundaries, and the game simply does not narrate that phrase mid-word.
processing.boundary_note: How a phrase is stopped at a word boundary. The word plays whole at full volume to the hold point and only then fades — fading into the boundary instead cost the last syllable. Hold and fade together stay inside the pause the aligner reports before the next word: half of it is held, the rest is the fade, so nothing reaches over the next word, which was audible as a hint of the letter to come. reach caps the pause that may be spent, so a long one is not sat through. The hold running past the aligner's end at all is deliberate — aligners mark the vowel, not the release after it.
processing.audit_note: How badly a clip may fit the text it was meant to say before `audit` doubts it. Forced alignment reports the fit, so a clip holding the wrong words scores badly — which is how the German UI shift and the early Czech cropped endings would have been caught without anyone listening to a hundred files. It cannot hear a wrong accent, only wrong words, so it flags rather than approves.

pricing_usd_per_1k_chars.note: Estimation only, for the plan report. RECHECK at https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/api before any production run — these change.

generate_guards.note: Refuses to spend more than this in one run unless the numbers are raised deliberately.

pricing_usd_per_hour_audio.note: Forced alignment is billed by audio duration at the speech-to-text rate, not by characters. RECHECK at https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/api — these change.

languages_note: A language records every category it has the data for. There is no per-language list to keep in step any more: German once shipped without 'ui' in its list and its title and menu names silently fell back to the device voice. Add a 'categories' key to a language only to deliberately restrict it.
retake_carrier_note: Which categories get carrier words on a retake. Short items only: a letter name or a UI fragment read alone trails off at its end, and a retake has no neighbours to lean on. A whole word is long enough to stand by itself, and wrapping one in carriers means cutting it back out of a three-item reading — which took 'letadýlko' and 'mrkvička' down to their last syllable.
